"Thats all I have right now, but Ill revisit this thread if I come up with anything more or see a good suggestion!  Remember, you dont need to be an established artist to make fursuit designs  theres plenty of F2U bases and guides! 💕💕  Good day ! 💕"

"Specific: Eyes Although its usually easy to see out of any coloured eyes, eyes with black are generally easier to see out of  typically featured in large pupils. So if you want better visibility and dont want huge eyes, using black is a good idea!"

"Specific: Hair More common in kemono fursuit designs, keep in mind that hair can be a little hard to recreate! Generally, its much easier for makers to make short/tied hair than long flowy hair. Its also easier to make hair with just one or two colours."

"General: Style As mentioned before, keep your makers in mind when designing a fursuit! For example, do you want a kemono, toony or realistic maker? If you want a toony fursuit, create your references only in this style and only go to toony makers. This helps with accuracy!"

"General: Shapes, Patterns, Motifs (2/2) Be aware of adding shapes such as complex polygons/images. Fursuits are 3D, not 2D! Flat shapes will need to be made onto a 3D plane, and may be harder to recreate. Image details may be lost, so for example dont use a small specific logo!"

"General: Shapes, Patterns, Motifs (1/2) A design may be cleaner and easier to create if you use basic shapes such as circles, triangles and squares in fur design. It also means youll come out with a less-chaotic and easy to read design!"

"General: Species If you have a very niche and/or complex species design, some makers may struggle to create your design. If you dont want a bland animal but also nothing too complex, go for simple hybrids or an easy to make open species!"

"General: Usage of white and black (3/3) Remember, dirt will show up very clearly on white! Its not a good idea to have white on soles, on palms and floor-dragging tails  unless youre prepared for extra washing! Lots of discolouration will happen, and very noticeably too."

"General: Usage of white and black (2/3) White is very bright and reflects a lot of light, and black is opposite. Large amounts of white is generally alright, but when paired with large amounts of black, you may get: [Dull white, void-like black] or [glowing white, fine black]."

"General: Usage of white and black (1/3) White and black are naturally common and pleasing colours, but you need to be careful with placement. Fine in moderation, but in large quantities it might look strange in pictures and when with other suits!"

"General: Clothing? Want to make your fursuit design compatible with clothing? Usually, a simpler design works better with clothing so your character isnt too "busy" or "imbalanced" looking. Have tons of torso patterns? This would all be hidden under a shirt! Keep that in mind!"

"General: Necks (2/2) Its a good idea NOT to put intricate designs on the neck, such as choker-like designs or designs intended for a slim neck. These will not translate well onto a fursuit. Its fine for art but if youre making a fursuit design, make it with a big neck in mind!"

"General: Necks (1/2) Youll notice that with fursuits, its rare to see slim necks. Thats because fursuit heads often include a dewlap/large neck, to hide the big hole you put your own head into! Also, they are made to help blend the head piece into the bodysuit."

"Design: Achievable? Please keep your makers in mind! Each one has their rules and limits. Dont go to a maker with a specific style, asking for another style they dont do. If a maker explicitly says they cannot do X, dont go to them with a design with X in it."

"Design: Recreating Remember that your design needs to be able to exist irl  sadly, things cannot defy gravity without wiring or support. Floating wings? Hard to pull off without being flimsy/fragile. Gradient fur? Hard to pull off without airbrushing, which can wash off easily."

"Design: Simplicity You know the phrase "Less is more"? For some fursuiters, this doesnt apply. But for others, this is important! Sometimes simpler designs are better than complex ones, because they are easier to make into fursuits and draw art for!"

"Colours: Availability Its a good idea to find out if the colours you want to use are available as faux fur colours. Sadly, not all colours exist in faux fur! If you have a certain maker in mind, go further and research what colours the suppliers they buy from have!"

"Colours: Number You may be tempted to throw on all of your fav colours, however a lot of the time this might not come out as well as you hoped. Not only can certain colours together look sickly, but more colours + intricacy =  more money for the fursuit! Try a set palette online!"
